title: Best AI Tools for COD Confirmation Calls & RTO Reduction in 2026
summary: Compare 8 AI platforms for automating COD confirmation calls and cutting RTO rates. Covers voice, SMS, WhatsApp, pricing, latency, and India readiness.
body_markdown:
Every COD order that ships without confirmation is a coin flip. Someone orders on impulse at 2 AM, forgets by Thursday, and refuses delivery on Saturday. That's an RTO, or return to origin: the shipment comes back and you eat the forward leg, the reverse leg, and the repackaging on top.


Here's the scale of it.[COD orders in Indian ecommerce come back at close to 26%, against under 2% for prepaid](https://www.gokwik.co/en_gb/blog/how-to-reduce-rto-in-e-commerce) . One confirmation call before dispatch catches the impulse buys, the address typos, and the junk entries before any of them cost you a shipment.


IVR and robocalls have done this for years, but they're rigid. A robocall can't hear hesitation in someone's voice, can't offer a prepaid discount mid-call to rescue a shaky order, and can't follow up on WhatsApp when nobody picks up. AI voice agents do all three. This piece compares 8 platforms on how well each one runs COD confirmation calls at scale, cuts RTO, and follows up when the call doesn't connect.


## TL;DR


-


Plivo is the strongest pick for D2C brands running COD confirmation at volume in India. Owned carrier network, voice plus SMS plus WhatsApp under one agent, and a direct Shopify connection so the agent reads the real order on the call.


-


Vapi suits developer-led teams who want to pick their own LLM, voice and transcription providers and wire the confirmation flow themselves.


-


Retell AI is the mid-market pick: batch calling, retry logic and structured post-call data without assembling the stack, plus a self-serve BAA.


-


Bland AI is built for high-volume outbound campaigns, which fits COD confirmation well if your orders are US-based.


-


Synthflow AI gets a non-technical ops lead calling by the afternoon, and the white-label tier makes it the obvious choice for agencies running confirmation calls for multiple clients.


-


ElevenLabs wins on voice quality, which matters when a robotic-sounding call gets hung up on before the customer confirms anything. Pairs well with Plivo's telephony.


-


Twilio makes sense if your stack already runs on it and you'd rather extend than migrate.


-


LiveKit is for developers building something past phone calls, into voice, video or other real-time experiences.


If you're calling COD orders at volume and want fewer moving parts between the order and the customer, Plivo is the one we'd shortlist first.


One note: DLT registration and DND scrubbing are your obligation whichever platform you pick. No vendor on this list does it for you.


## What Actually Matters for COD Confirmation Calls


Six things separate a platform that runs COD confirmation in production from one that demos well and falls over at 5,000 orders a day.


### 1. India telephony coverage and reliability


Your calls are dialling Indian mobile numbers, so the platform needs to provision Indian numbers or connect via SIP to Indian carriers, and route cleanly across Jio, Airtel and Vi. Platforms that rent telephony from a third party add a network hop, which costs you latency and adds a second vendor to chase when calls start failing on a dispatch morning. Ask for connection rates on Indian mobile traffic specifically, not a global average, and ask what happens when a carrier route degrades.


### 2. End-to-end call latency


Confirmation calls run 30 to 60 seconds, so there's no room for the agent to think. A PNAS study by Stivers et al. across 10 languages found humans hand off conversational turns in roughly 200ms. Above 800ms, callers notice the pause. Above 1,500ms, the conversation breaks down and people hang up. Sub-500ms end-to-end is the target. Every hop in the path adds to it, which is why platforms that own the carrier layer tend to land lower than ones stitching three vendors together.


### 3. Outbound campaign infrastructure


This is the one that breaks at volume. You dispatch in batches, so you call in batches, and the platform has to push a few thousand orders through without you babysitting it. Check three things: how many concurrent lines your plan actually includes rather than the platform's theoretical maximum, whether batch calling is native or something you build, and whether retry logic is configurable (try again in four hours, then tomorrow morning, then stop). Several platforms here were built inbound-first and treat outbound campaigns as a bolt-on.


### 4. Omnichannel follow-up


Most confirmation calls won't be answered, and that's normal. What matters is what happens next. A no-answer that rolls into a WhatsApp message with the order details and a confirm button recovers orders that a voice-only tool writes off. The same applies after a successful call: a written record with a tracking link gives the buyer something to reply to if the address is wrong. Look for shared context across channels, so the WhatsApp message knows a call already went out and doesn't start from scratch.


### 5. Conversational intelligence, and whether the agent knows the order


An agent saying "we're calling about your recent order" gets hung up on. One saying "confirming two units, ₹1,840, to the Andheri East address" gets a real answer. That needs live order data at call time, either through a native Shopify or WooCommerce connection or an API call mid-conversation. Ask specifically whether the agent can fetch data during the call or only receive variables passed in at the start.


On top of that, the agent should handle what an IVR can't: catch hesitation, read the address back for correction, offer a prepaid discount to rescue a shaky order, and flag suspicious signals like a mismatched pin code or an address that's already RTO'd twice. That's where the actual RTO reduction comes from.


### 6. Compliance: DLT, DND, and payment data


This is the criterion teams discover late, and for India-focused calling it's the binding one. Automated outbound calls sit under TRAI's TCCCPR framework, which means registration on the DLT platform and scrubbing against DND and NCPR preferences before you dial.


A confirmation call about an order the customer placed is transactional, and transactional communication is treated differently from promotional. The moment your agent offers a 5% prepaid discount mid-call, that boundary gets blurry. Worth getting a view from counsel on how your script is classified before you scale it, because the answer changes what you're allowed to say to a DND-registered number.


On the data side, PCI DSS matters if you're taking payment on the call, SOC 2 matters for anyone doing security review, and DPDP Act obligations apply to the customer data you're processing regardless. Check that whatever a vendor lists covers the voice product and outbound specifically, not just their platform in general.

### Plivo


Plivo has been running communications infrastructure for 15 years, and it owns its carrier network across 190+ countries including India. The AI agent layer sits inside that infrastructure rather than on top of it, so the agent runtime, the audio path and the phone network are one system.


For COD confirmation that means the call dials an Indian mobile on Plivo's own network, the agent confirms the order conversationally, and the same agent follows up with an SMS receipt and a WhatsApp message carrying tracking details. One conversation history across all three. No stitching separate voice, SMS and WhatsApp tools together, which matters more than it sounds when most of your calls won't be answered and WhatsApp is where you actually get the confirmation.


It also removes the extra hop that voice AI startups add when they rent telephony from someone else. That hop costs latency and gives you a second vendor to chase when calls start failing on a dispatch morning.


#### Key features


-


Owned carrier network in 150+ countries including India, with sub-500ms end-to-end latency and 99.99% uptime


-


Voice, SMS and WhatsApp as one agent with shared context, so a no-answer rolls into a WhatsApp confirmation without you building the handoff


-


Vibe Agent lets ops describe the confirmation script in plain English; Agent Studio is the drag-and-drop canvas for tweaking it; the Voice API is there in Python, Node, Go and REST when you need custom logic like address verification or a prepaid conversion offer


-


Built-in eval framework that scores calls against your defined goals and surfaces failing patterns, so you find the broken Hindi prompt before 2,000 calls, not after


-


50+ languages, which covers the regional coverage most Indian D2C brands need


-


Inbound and outbound with equal depth, so customers calling back about their order land somewhere useful


-


HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS Level 1, GDPR and CSA STAR, with data residency in the US, EU and APAC, AES-256 at rest and TLS in transit


#### Limitations


Human handoff specifics like queue management and skills-based routing aren't documented publicly, so ask during evaluation if your escalation path is complicated. The pre-built integration catalog is narrower than Twilio's, which means more implementation work if you're connecting Salesforce, Zendesk and a custom OMS. There's no documented white-label agency programme, so agencies running voice for multiple D2C clients are better served by Synthflow.


The plan split is the main thing to check. Pay-as-you-go covers the US and India, caps at 50 concurrent calls and $2,500 of monthly usage. Broader coverage, WhatsApp, custom concurrency and BAA/HIPAA all sit in Enterprise at $1,000/month. At 1,000+ COD calls a day you'll hit the concurrency ceiling, so price the Enterprise contract rather than the headline rate.


Worth noting that DLT registration and DND scrubbing are your obligation regardless of platform. Plivo supports Indian traffic, but no vendor on this list registers your headers and templates for you.


### Vapi


Vapi is for teams who'd rather assemble the stack than buy it. You pick the speech-to-text provider, the LLM, the voice and the telephony carrier, then wire them together through Vapi's orchestration layer. For COD confirmation that's useful if you want a cheap fast model handling the yes/no script and something better handling the prepaid conversion pitch, which bundled platforms won't let you split. The tradeoff is that you're the integrator now, and when calls start failing you're working out whether it was the carrier, the STT or the orchestration.


#### Key features


-


Swap any layer: OpenAI, Anthropic, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Azure and others, tuned per call type


-


API-first with proper control over call flow, tools and webhooks


-


Supports 1,000+ concurrent sessions, which covers dispatch-day bursts once you've paid for the lines


-


SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS v4 and GDPR, with HIPAA available as an add-on


#### Limitations


The $0.05/min platform fee tells you almost nothing, since your real cost depends on four vendors you picked. Concurrency bites too: 10 lines included, then $10 per line per month, which adds up fast when you're batch-calling COD orders. There's no no-code builder, so every script tweak goes through a developer.


### Retell AI


Retell sits in the middle of this list, which for COD confirmation is a sensible place to be. Developers can shape the flow, but you don't have to assemble the voice stack yourself to get an agent dialling. Batch calling, retry logic, human transfer and post-call analysis all come in the box. The useful bit for COD is the structured extraction: the agent pulls defined fields off the call, so "confirmed, wants Tuesday delivery, address corrected to flat 402" lands in your OMS instead of a transcript nobody reads. Compliance is unusually easy here too, with a BAA you can sign yourself rather than negotiate.


#### Key features


-


Building, testing, deploying and monitoring in one place, so less infrastructure to stand up before your first batch goes out


-


Structured data off every call: summaries, sentiment and custom extracted fields that write back to your store


-


Use Retell's telephony or bring your own via SIP, Twilio or Telnyx


-


SOC 2 Type I and II, HIPAA, GDPR and ISO 27001, with a self-serve BAA at no extra fee


#### Limitations


Retell doesn't own the PSTN layer, so your calls still run through a third-party carrier and PCI coverage depends on which one. Phone numbers are US-concentrated, so Indian numbers mean bringing your own SIP trunk and carrying the DLT registration yourself.


### Bland AI


Bland is the outbound specialist here, which suits COD confirmation since the whole job is outbound. It's built for pushing large contact lists through the phone network fast, and it runs its own voice, language and speech models rather than routing your call data through OpenAI or Anthropic. For a brand calling every COD order at dispatch, the scale story is the draw: high concurrency, batch campaigns, voicemail detection and warm transfers all come standard rather than being something you assemble.


#### Key features


-


Built for volume outbound, with batch campaigns designed around large contact lists rather than one-off calls


-


Voice, language and speech models run in-house, so call data doesn't pass through third-party AI providers


-


Call-centre plumbing included: live and warm transfers, voicemail detection, multilingual conversations, retry handling


-


SOC 2 Type I and II, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI DSS 4.0.1


#### Limitations


API-first with no no-code builder, so anything past a basic confirmation script needs engineering time. Pricing isn't purely usage-based either: plans start at $299/month and the subscription doesn't include calling minutes. Transfers, failed outbound attempts and TTS all bill separately, which matters when most COD confirmation calls won't connect.


Telephony is third-party and US-focused, so Indian numbers mean bringing your own SIP trunk, with DLT registration sitting on your side.


### Synthflow AI


Synthflow is the one your ops lead can actually run. It's a genuine no-code builder, so someone who knows which objections cause an RTO can build the confirmation flow, connect it to your store, and have it calling by the afternoon. That matters for COD work, where the script keeps changing as you learn what makes people refuse delivery. The white-label tier also makes it the obvious pick if you're an agency running confirmation calling for several D2C clients rather than one brand running it for itself.


#### Key features


-


Visual builder non-technical people can use, with multi-step flows covering CRM lookups, order checks and post-call actions


-


White-label and sub-accounts, so agencies can rebrand it and run multiple clients from one workspace


-


200+ integrations, including the CRMs, ticketing and scheduling tools most D2C stacks already run on


-


SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS, with regional data tenants in the US and EU


#### Limitations


No developer escape hatch, so outgrowing the templates means moving platforms rather than dropping into an API. Latency and reliability complaints show up at higher volumes, which is worth testing before you commit to dispatch-day batches.


The add-ons are where the price actually lives: Performance Routing and Low Latency Edge are $0.04/min each, phone numbers are $1.50/month, and white-label runs $2,000/month. Telephony is primarily US, so Indian numbers mean bringing your own trunk and handling DLT yourself.


### ElevenLabs


ElevenLabs made its name on voice quality, and ElevenAgents extends that into live phone calls. For COD confirmation that's worth more than it sounds. A call that sounds obviously robotic gets hung up on in three seconds, and a hang-up is an unconfirmed order that ships anyway. If your calls go out in Hindi, Tamil or Marathi and you need them to sound like a person rather than an IVR, this is the strongest voice layer on the list. What it isn't is a calling platform. You're bringing your own telephony and building the order logic around it.


#### Key features


-


Best voice on the list: natural delivery, low latency, voice cloning, all of which directly move your answer and completion rates


-


32+ languages with in-conversation code-switching, useful when a customer answers in one language and switches mid-call


-


Connects via Twilio or SIP, so you're not replacing your existing telephony


-


SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS and several ISO certifications


#### Limitations


Telephony is somebody else's bill, so the subscription isn't your cost per call, and LLM usage bills separately on top. It's a voice layer rather than a confirmation product, so batch campaigns, retry logic and writing back to your store are all things you build.


No owned network means Indian numbers come through a third-party carrier, with DLT registration sitting wherever those numbers do.


### Twilio


Twilio is the safe answer if your stack already runs on it. ConversationRelay handles the real-time speech and call orchestration while you bring your own LLM and business logic, so your existing numbers, routing and carrier relationships carry straight over. For a D2C brand already sending order updates through Twilio SMS, adding COD confirmation calls is an extension rather than a migration. The catch is that Twilio gives you infrastructure, not a finished confirmation agent, so somebody on your team is building the part that actually knows about orders.


#### Key features


-


Carrier-grade owned network with global reach, number provisioning and routing in-house, including Indian numbers


-


Bring your own LLM, so you're not locked to one AI vendor and can control cost per call type


-


Voice, SMS and WhatsApp all exist here, even though they're wired as separate APIs


-


SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS and ISO 27001, plus a name your procurement team won't question


#### Limitations


Everything requires code. No no-code builder, so a working agent means stitching Voice, STT, LLM, TTS and your own orchestration together. The channels are separate APIs rather than one agent with shared context, so a WhatsApp fallback after a missed confirmation call is something you build and maintain.


### LiveKit


LiveKit is the most developer-shaped option here and the least like something you'd buy off the shelf. It gives you real-time infrastructure and an agent framework, then leaves the actual agent to you. For most D2C teams running COD confirmation that's more rope than you need, since the job is a 30-second scripted call, not a bespoke real-time application. It earns its place if you're building something past phone calls, because it's the only option here handling voice, video and screen sharing through one framework.


#### Key features


-


Low-latency audio transport is the core of the product, not a layer bolted on top


-


Genuinely multimodal: voice, video and data channels in one framework, which nothing else here offers


-


Pick your own STT, LLM and TTS, or use LiveKit Inference to keep it simple


-


Apache 2.0 open source core, so you can self-host for strict data residency and avoid lock-in


#### Limitations


You're building the agent yourself, including turn detection, interruption handling, tool calling and error recovery. That's weeks of work before your first confirmation call goes out.


PSTN works through SIP but you're typically bringing your own trunk, so Indian telephony is another vendor relationship with DLT sitting on your side. Compliance is tier-gated too: SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA only land on the Scale plan at $500/month, which rules out the cheaper tiers for regulated data.


## Choosing the Right Tool for Your COD Setup


The right platform comes down to daily COD volume, how technical your team is, and whether you need anything beyond voice.


Running 1,000+ COD confirmations a day across India?


You need owned telephony in India, omnichannel follow-up, and ops able to change scripts without filing a ticket. Plivo is the only platform here that does all three. The $1,000/month entry point stops looking expensive once you price a five-point RTO reduction against thousands of daily shipments. It also connects to Shopify and WooCommerce directly, so the agent can read the actual order on the call instead of a variable someone passed in.


Outbound-heavy and cost-sensitive?


Bland's dialing engine is purpose-built for volume campaigns. Telephony is third-party and US-focused though, so Indian numbers mean bringing your own trunk. Strongest fit if your COD orders are US-based.


Mid-market, want it running this month?


Retell gets you batch calling, retry logic and structured post-call data without assembling the stack, and the self-serve BAA means no procurement call. You're still bringing your own SIP trunk for India.


Developer team that wants full control?


Vapi. Pick your LLM, STT and TTS and wire them yourself. The cost is that ops can't touch the confirmation flow without a developer, and you'll need a separate tool for SMS and WhatsApp follow-up.


Under 200 COD orders a day, or an agency?


Synthflow. A non-technical person can have a confirmation bot live in an afternoon, and the white-label tier is the reason agencies pick it. The ceiling is real: prepaid conversion logic, API address verification, or scale past a few hundred daily calls and you're moving platforms.


Already all-in on Twilio?


You have India telephony and enterprise compliance already, so it's a build-versus-switch call. Building a conversational confirmation agent on Twilio means assembling components and writing orchestration. If your engineering team has capacity, adding AI inside Twilio avoids a migration. For net-new, Plivo ships faster.


Want the calls to sound genuinely human?


Use ElevenLabs voices on Plivo. The integration is first-party, so you get ElevenLabs' voice quality with Plivo's telephony, omnichannel and compliance underneath.

## Frequently Asked Questions


Does a confirmation call actually cut RTO?


Yes, when it's part of a real verification flow rather than a call on its own. Brands running pre-dispatch confirmation alongside address checks and COD-to-prepaid nudges report cutting RTO 30 to 45 percent within 90 days. The call catches impulse orders and address errors. The prepaid conversion is what moves the number hardest, since prepaid comes back at under 2% against COD's 26%.


Is it legal to make automated calls to Indian mobile numbers?


You'll need DLT registration and DND scrubbing under TRAI's TCCCPR framework, and that obligation sits with you regardless of which platform you pick. A confirmation call about an order the customer placed is transactional, which is treated differently from promotional. The moment your agent offers a prepaid discount mid-call, that line gets blurry. Worth a view from counsel before you scale.


What does a confirmation call cost per order?


Model cost per confirmed order, not cost per minute. These calls run 30 to 60 seconds and most won't connect, so you're paying minimums on more misses than hits. At a 40% connect rate with retries, budget roughly $0.13 per confirmed order. Against ₹350 to ₹700 per RTO, that maths comfortably.


Do these tools handle Hindi and regional languages?


Hindi is well covered everywhere. Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali and Kannada are where quality thins out, and there's a real gap between a language being technically supported and it sounding like a person. Test your specific languages on real confirmation scripts before committing.


Can the agent see the actual order?


Depends on the platform, and this is the thing to check hardest. You want an agent that can pull live order data mid-call, not just receive variables passed in when the call starts. Plivo connects to Shopify and WooCommerce directly. Most others need you to build the integration.


Do I need developers for this?


Not always. Synthflow is genuinely no-code and Retell gives you a visual builder alongside an API. Vapi, LiveKit and Twilio all need engineering time. Plivo sits in between, with plain-English agent building for ops and an API when you outgrow it.
